meta.title: About — Emmanuel Forcelledo, founder of Forcelis
meta.description: A Mexican economist (UNAM) who has worked in finance, planning, supply chain and data in Mexico, Canada and Japan, helping foreign companies decide where and how to enter Mexico.

hero.title: Hi, I'm Emmanuel Forcelledo.
hero.subtitle: I help foreign companies make the call on Mexico before they invest: which market, which region, and how to enter.

bio.title: Where this comes from
paragraphs: I'm a Mexican economist (UNAM) who has worked in finance, planning, supply chain and data in Mexico, Canada and Japan.
My research focused on why some Mexican regions grow and others don't. Forcelis helps foreign companies make that same call before they invest in Mexico.
bio.languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian and Japanese.

items.title: I never invent a number
items.body: If something can't be measured with the data available, I say so. A figure that looks reasonable but isn't measured is worse than none, because you'll make a decision with it.

items.title: Every finding comes with an action
items.body: An observation that doesn't change a decision isn't a deliverable. Each finding comes with what to do about it.

items.title: If Mexico isn't the right move, I tell you
items.body: A study can conclude that the timing, the region or the channel is wrong. That answer is worth more than an optimistic one.

notUs.title: What Forcelis doesn't do
items: No legal, tax or immigration advice. When a project needs it, we work with local partners.
No national averages dressed up as a recommendation: every conclusion is regional.
No invented market sizes: every figure is sourced and dated.

closing.title: Thinking about Mexico?
closing.body: Let's talk for 20 minutes about what you're evaluating, and I'll tell you honestly whether a study makes sense.
